paragraph: Oakland is a single-family market, plain and simple. Fifty-three homes sold over six months at a median of $700,000 against a median list of $650,000, with a sale-to-list ratio of 1.06, roughly 72 percent closing above asking, and a median of 14 days on market. That is a real seller's market, and buyers should expect competition on the good ones. The typical sale is a three-bedroom with two full baths, mostly ranches, colonials, and capes. Sales ran from $284,888 to $2,065,000, so the median is the number to anchor on. The monthly series shows volume building into summer with 14 closings in June and 12 in July, and the July median of $865,500 is the highest reading since a thin March. That is a market tracking the normal summer peak, not softening. If Oakland follows the usual arc, expect the median to drift back down through fall while closings stay steady until deep winter thins them out.
